pullRequest.title: feat: implement FR-12 local login gate (T-08)

implementationOverview:
PR #5 implements FR-12 (local login gate): first-use setup (create username + passcode), later login, and logout. Credentials are stored in localStorage as a salted SHA-256 hash (never plaintext) under a dedicate key, and the authenticated state is represented only by a sessionStorage flag (tab-scoped). The contact manager UI
  is not mounted into the DOM until authenticated, and is fully unmounted again on logout.
reviewedComponents: src/main.ts (auth gate mount/unmount, logout wiring, unsaved changes warning lifecycle)
tests/integration/auth-state.test.ts (session, gating, generic error, crypto unavailable)

CR-01.evidence: src/auth/auth-state.ts rejects whitespace-only username/passcode on setup, and trims username on setup and login; integration tests cover whitespace scenarios.

CR-03.evidence: src/auth/crypto.ts adds isCryptoAvailable(); auth-state catches crypto errors and transitions to 'unavailable' state.

CR-04.evidence: src/ui/login-view.ts username input has autocapitalize=off and spellcheck=false.

FIND-001.evidence: src/ui/login-view.ts does not interpolate disclosure text into innerHTML; it sets it via textContent.

FIND-002.evidence: src/auth/auth-state.ts wraps generateSalt/hashPasscode in try/catch and sets unavailable state with user-friendly message.

FIND-003.evidence: tests/unit/auth-crypto.test.ts uses vi.stubGlobal('crypto', undefined) and vi.unstubAllGlobals() for isolation.

reviewFindings.evidenceSection: catch (error) { ... currentView = "contact" // Mark as mounted to prevent duplicate attempts }
reviewFindings.description: On contact manager mount failure, the app renders a fallback error UI but sets currentView to "contact". This can prevent any future remount attempt in the same tab session (even after logout/re-login) until a page reload.
reviewFindings.whyItMatters: Recoverability: a transient failure or partial state can leave the app stuck on an error screen. FR-12 expects logout/login to be reliable recovery mechanism.
reviewFindings.recommendedCorrection: Use a distinct view state (e.g. "error") or leave currentView as "login"/"none" and allow a subsequent auth-to-authed transition to retry mounting. Consider adding a "Retry loading" action.

reviewFindings.description: The fallback error markup uses innerHTML. It is constant today (no interpolation), which is good. Keep it that way to avoid futurh xss regressions.
reviewFindings.whyItMatters: Mitigates future regression risk when templates later get dynamic content.
reviewFindings.recommendedCorrection: Unless necessary, prefer building DOM nodes via document.createElement() and textContent or keep the HTML string constant as rectified.

securityObservations: Credential storage uses a salted SHA-256 hash; plaintext passcode is never persisted.
Passcode is cleared on failed login attempts in login-view.ts
Contact UI is not mounted pre-auth; DOM gatekeeping reduces accidental data exposure.
Web Crypto unavailability is handled with a controlled unavailable state.
potentialRegressionAreas: Mount/unmount lifecycle in src/main.ts (especially failure fallback)
Unsaved changes warning install/cleanup when toggling between authenticated and login UIs
Tests that pre-seed auth via addInitScript should continue to exist along real login-flow tests (auth.spec.ts does test real flows)

positive: First-use setup: credate credential, authenticate, and unlock contact UIB
Later login: correct username+passcode unlocks contact UI, session persists across reload in same tab
Logout: clears session flag, keeps credential and contacts in localStorage
negative: Wrong username vs wrong passcode: both show the exact same generic error (Invalid username or passcode.)
Pre-login: contact data/controls not present in DOM (DOM gating)
Crypto unavailable: app shows 'Sign-in is currently unavailable' panel, does not crash
edge: Rapid logout/re-login cycles do not duplicate Ui mounts or listeners
Contact manager mount failure: verify user can logout from fallback and subsequent login can recover (see CR-PR-001)
New-tab: fresh tab requires login even with stored credential

notes: This review was performed via GitHub API static inspection. No tests were executed by the reviewer in this step.
